reconcile.connective: Harmonizers argue John names only Mary Magdalene by editorial selection, while the fuller lists assume the same larger group of women.

discrepancy.connective: The objection was pressed by H. S. Reimarus, who listed the differing counts—one in John, two in Matthew, three in Mark, more in Luke—as evidence the resurrection reports cannot be reconciled.

skeptic.name: Hermann Samuel Reimarus
skeptic.work: Fragments (On the Intention of Jesus and His Disciples), ed. G. E. Lessing
skeptic.attribution: Hermann Samuel Reimarus (d. 1768), Fragments, posthumously published by G. E. Lessing (1774-78)

excerpts.excerpt_text: John only mentions Mary of Magdala, because he appears to wish to give a more detailed history of her conduct than of any of the rest; but the other evangelists speak of three persons who went together to the tomb, viz. Mary of Magdala, Mary the mother of James, and Salome: Mat 28:1; Mar 16:1.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the number-of-women tension: explains John's single woman as selective focus on Mary Magdalene while affirming the synoptic group of three went together.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's harmonizing treatment of the resurrection narratives addresses the differing lists of women at the sepulchre directly, arguing each evangelist names a subset of the same company.

link.note: No allowlisted page found that treats the number-of-women discrepancy specifically; gotquestions.org/resurrection-accounts.html addresses appearances and angels but not the women count, so omitted rather than mismatched.
